summary: This note is a clipped RNIB (Royal National Institute of Blind People) website page whose body is almost entirely site navigation menus, cookie-style boilerplate and repeated appearance toggles. The only lighting-related items are a menu entry titled 'Lighting' under 'Independent living' and a 'Light sensitivity (photophobia)' page under eye conditions. The note contains no substantive lighting guidance, so its informational value is limited to showing how RNIB organises these topics.
one_line: Clipped RNIB web navigation page; its only lighting items are a 'Lighting' page under Independent living and a light sensitivity (photophobia) condition page.
key_facts: The note is titled 'lighting' and its source is listed as 'bright' with domain 'biology'.
The page is a clipped RNIB website page, and most of its text is navigation menus rather than article content.
RNIB's site menu lists 'Lighting' as a subsection under 'Independent living', alongside 'Help with low vision', 'Practical adaptations', 'Labelling', 'Cooking' and 'Adapting your home'.
The 'Your eyes' menu lists 'Light sensitivity (photophobia)' as an eye condition page.
The 'Light sensitivity (photophobia)' page has a sub-page titled 'Five steps to getting the right glasses for light sensitivity'.
The 'How to keep your eyes healthy' section lists 'Protect your eyes from the sun' as a page.
The eye conditions menu includes Age-related macular degeneration (AMD), Cataracts, Glaucoma and Colour Vision Deficiency (CVD), also known as colour blindness.
The 'Independent living' section includes 'Safety at home' and 'Reduce your risk of falls' among its listed pages.
The 'Living with sight loss' section includes 'Assistive aids and technology' with sub-pages such as 'Smart technology for the home' and 'Navigation technology'.
The menu lists 'RNIB Helpline' and 'Sight loss counselling' under 'Community connection and wellbeing'.
The note includes the repeated phrase 'Switch colour mode' with options Light, Dark and Yellow, which is website display boilerplate.
The note gives no lighting recommendations, measurements or explanations of how lighting affects vision.
